subject: Taxes
title: How Credits Beat Deductions
description: A 60-second lesson on How Credits Beat Deductions.

hook.text: A $1,000 deduction saves you $220 if you're in the 22% bracket. A $1,000 credit saves you exactly $1,000.

buildup.text: Deductions reduce your taxable income. Credits reduce your actual tax bill dollar for dollar.

discovery.text: Some credits are 'refundable'—if the credit exceeds what you owe, the government sends you the difference as a check.

twist.text: The Earned Income Tax Credit gives low-income workers up to $7,430.

climax.text: Tax credits are welfare programs disguised as tax provisions.

punchline.text: Deductions reduce income. Credits reduce tax. Dollar for dollar, credits win.

quiz.question: How does a tax credit differ from a tax deduction?
options: Credits reduce your tax bill dollar for dollar; deductions reduce taxable income
